facts.statement: Fossils of Shastasaurus have been discovered in the United States, Canada, and China.
facts.quote: Specimens have been found in the United States, Canada, and China.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus sikanniensis had a ribcage less than 2 meters deep despite a flipper-to-flipper distance of over 7 meters.
facts.quote: S. sikanniensis had a ribcage slightly less than 2 m deep despite a distance of over 7 m between its flippers.

facts.statement: Researchers proposed that Shastasaurus was a suction feeder preying on soft-bodied cephalopods due to its unusually short, toothless snout.
facts.quote: With its unusually short, toothless snout (compared to the longer, toothed, dolphin-like snouts of most ichthyosaurs), it had been proposed that Shastasaurus was a suction feeder (or filled a similar ecological niche as extant beaked whales), preying primarily on soft-bodied cephalopods.

facts.statement: Current research suggests Shastasaurus jaws may not have been adapted for suction feeding because their hyoid bones were unsuitable for impact forces and related species possessed teeth and gut contents indicating a different diet.
facts.quote: However, current research indicates that the jaws of shastasaurid ichthyosaurs do not fit the suction-feeding profile, since their short and narrow hyoid bones are unsuitable to withstand impact forces for such kind of feeding, and since some species like Shonisaurus had robust sectorial teeth with gut contents of mollusk shells and vertebrates.

facts.statement: It is unknown whether Shastasaurus possessed a dorsal fin, though the basal ichthyosaur Mixosaurus did.
facts.quote: It is unknown whether Shastasaurus had a dorsal fin; however, the smaller, more basal ichthyosaur Mixosaurus had one.

facts.statement: The upper tail fluke of Shastasaurus was likely much less developed than the shark-like tails found in later ichthyosaur species.
facts.quote: The upper fluke of the tail was probably much less-developed than the shark-like tails found in later species.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus pacificus is known only from fragmentary remains, leading to the assumption that it had normal ichthyosaur proportions.
facts.quote: It is known only from fragmentary remains, which have led to the assumption that it was a 'normal' ichthyosaur in terms of proportions, especially skull proportions.

facts.statement: Complete skulls of Shastasaurus liangae show an unusual short and toothless snout.
facts.quote: Complete skulls show that it had an unusual short and toothless snout.

facts.statement: A 2013 discovery of a juvenile specimen suggested that Guanlingsaurus (formerly Shastasaurus liangae) should be considered a distinct genus due to its shorter hyoid bone.
facts.quote: However, a new juvenile specimen discovered in 2013 shows that the hyoid bone of Guanlingsaurus is much shorter, and considered it as a distinct genus based on phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: The classification of Shastasaurus sikanniensis remains debated, with analyses in 2013, 2019, and 2021 yielding conflicting results regarding its relationship to Shonisaurus versus Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: However, a 2013 analysis supported the original classification, finding it more closely related to Shonisaurus than to Shastasaurus. In the 2019 study, S. sikanniensis was pertained within the genus Shastasaurus. In the 2021 analysis, S. sikanniensis forms a clade with Shonisaurus, indicating that it is closer to Shonisaurus than to Shastasaurus.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus has been interpreted as a specialized predator of fish and shell-less cephalopods that hunted using suction.
facts.quote: Este animal ha sido interpretado como un especializado devorador de peces y cefalópodos sin concha, que atrapaba través de la succión.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus lived during the Triassic period.
facts.quote: Shastasaurus vivió durante el periodo Triásico.

facts.statement: If Shastasaurus sikanniensis is correctly classified within the genus, it would be the largest species, reaching 21 meters in length.
facts.quote: Si la especie S. sikkanniensis efectivamente pertenecía a Shastasaurus, sería la mayor especie, llegando a medir 21 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus was an animal with a very slender profile.
facts.quote: Era un animal de perfil bastante delgado.

facts.statement: In the largest specimens, the ribcage was less than 2 meters high despite a trunk flipper distance of nearly 7 meters.
facts.quote: En los mayores especímenes la caja torácica medía menos de 2 metros de alto, a pesar de tener una distancia de cerca de 7 metros entre las aletas de su tronco.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus had an unusually short skull with a blunt, toothless snout, distinct from the elongated, toothed dolphin-like snouts of most other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: Su cráneo además era inusualmente corto, con un hocico trunco y desdentado, muy distinto a los hocicos alargados y dentados, similares a los de los delfines, que tenían la práctica totalidad de los demás ictiosaurios.

facts.statement: The short snout suggests Shastasaurus was likely a suction feeder that ate mainly soft-bodied cephalopods lacking shells for defense.
facts.quote: Parece probable entonces que este extraño hocico indique que el Shastasaurus era un devorador por succión, alimentándose sobre todo de cefalópodos de cuerpo blando, que carecían de conchas para defenderse.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus likely created a sudden water flow to suck prey into its open mouth by rapidly opening its jaws and pulling its tongue back.
facts.quote: Mediante la rápida apertura de la boca y tirando de la lengua, creaba un flujo repentino de agua que absorbía a su presa en sus fauces abiertas.

facts.statement: The part of the Shastasaurus skull containing the jaw-opening muscles was particularly large.
facts.quote: La parte de su cráneo donde se situaban los músculos de apertura de la mandíbula era particularmente grande.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus had large hyoid bones that allowed it to pull its tongue back abruptly.
facts.quote: También tenía grandes huesos hioides, que le permitían recoger su lengua hacia atrás bruscamente.

facts.statement: In Shastasaurus liangae, the skull comprised only 8.3% of total body length (9.3% in a juvenile specimen).
facts.quote: En S. liangae, la única especie con varios cráneos bien preservados, el cráneo solo contenía un 8.3% de la longitud corporal total (9.3% en un ejemplar juvenil).

facts.statement: Unlike its relative Shonisaurus, even juvenile Shastasaurus specimens were completely toothless.
facts.quote: A diferencia de su pariente Shonisaurus, incluso los jóvenes Shastasaurus carecían por completo de dientes.

facts.statement: The Shastasaurus snout was quite compressed due to a unique arrangement of cranial bones.
facts.quote: El hocico estaba bastante comprimido a través de una disposición única de los huesos craneales.

facts.statement: Unlike many other reptiles, the nasal bone in Shastasaurus extended to the snout tip, and all snout bones narrowed abruptly.
facts.quote: A diferencia de muchos otros reptiles, el hueso nasal, que usualmente forma la parte media del cráneo, se extendía hasta la punta del hocico, y todos los huesos del hocico se estrechaban abruptamente.

facts.statement: Other shastasaurids likely lacked dorsal fins, and there is no concrete evidence supporting the presence of a dorsal fin in any Shastasaurus species.
facts.quote: No obstante, otros shastasáuridos probablemente carecían de aletas dorsales, y no hay ninguna evidencia concreta que apoye la presencia de dicha aleta en alguna de sus especies.

facts.statement: The type species of Shastasaurus is S. pacificus, which lived during the late Carnian period in northern California.
facts.quote: La especie tipo de Shastasaurus es S. pacificus, del periodo Carniense tardío del norte de California.

facts.statement: S. pacificus is known only from very fragmentary remains, leading to the assumption that it was a 'normal' ichthyosaur with standard body proportions, especially in the skull.
facts.quote: Es conocido sólo de restos muy fragmentarios, lo que llevó a asumir que era un ictiosaurio 'normal' en términos de proporciones corporales, especialmente las del cráneo.

facts.statement: Shastasaurus liangae was the first species to definitively show that Shastasaurus was an animal with distinctive short snouts and toothless jaws.
facts.quote: Shastasaurus liangae fue la primera especie que definitivamente mostró que era Shastasaurus era un animal de distintivos hocico corto y mandíbulas desdentadas.

facts.statement: The largest specimen of Shastasaurus liangae measures 8.3 meters in length.
facts.quote: El mayor espécimen (YIGMR SPCV03109) mide 8.3 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: A juvenile specimen of Shastasaurus liangae was found measuring approximately 3.74 meters in length.
facts.quote: Un ejemplar juvenil (YIGMR SPCV03108) también fue hallado, midiendo unos 3.74 metros de largo.

facts.statement: S. sikkanniensis was originally described in 2004 as a giant species of the genus Shonisaurus.
facts.quote: S. sikkanniensis fue originalmente descrito en 2004 como una especie gigante del género Shonisaurus.

facts.statement: A 2011 study supported the hypothesis that S. sikkanniensis was more closely related to Shastasaurus than to Shonisaurus, leading to its reclassification as Shastasaurus sikkanniensis.
facts.quote: El primer estudio que examinó estas relaciones, hecho en 2011, apoyó la hipótesis de que esta especie estaba más relacionada con Shastasaurus que a Shonisaurus, por lo que se la reclasificó como Shastasaurus sikkanniensis.

facts.statement: However, a 2013 analysis supported the original classification, finding that the species is more closely related to Shonisaurus than to Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un análisis de 2013 apoyó la clasificación original, encontrando que está más cercanamente relacionado con Shonisaurus que a Shastasaurus.

facts.statement: In 2009, Shang and Li reclassified the species Guizhouichthyosaurus tangae as Shastasaurus tangae.
facts.quote: En 2009, Shang & Li reclasificaron la especie Guizhouichthyosaurus tangae como Shastasaurus tangae.

facts.statement: However, later analyses showed that Guizhouichthyosaurus was actually more closely related to advanced ichthyosaurs and cannot be considered a species of Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, análisis posteriores mostraron que Guizhouichthyosaurus estaba de hecho más emparentado con los ictiosaurios más avanzados, y no puede ser considerado una especie de Shastasaurus.

facts.statement: Doubtful species referred to this genus include S. carinthiacus from the Austrian Alps and S. neubigi from the Muschelkalk in Germany.
facts.quote: Especies dudosas que han sido referidas a este género incluyen S. carinthiacus (Huene, 1925) de los Alpes austríacos y S. neubigi (Sander, 1997) de Muschelkalk en Alemania.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Shastasaurus is Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Shastasauridae

facts.statement: The family of the genus Shastasaurus is Shastasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Shastasauridae

facts.statement: The genus Shastasaurus belongs to the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The genus Shastasaurus lived from the Carnian to the Norian periods, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Shastasaurus in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 10
